content:
Krail stands with the pen balanced between two fingers, its nib pointing at the blank approval space the way a compass needle finds north.

"The household expects a decision by the evening ledger, my lord," he says. "An open fire in Lady Ilyra's wing, a missing folio, and a servant's daughter admitting unauthorized entry — the accounts will not balance themselves while we wait on sentiment."

Liora's breath goes quick and shallow. Elise's hand finds her daughter's shoulder and stays there, the bandaged forearm held stiffly at her side.

"My lord," Elise says, and her voice is steadier than her clasped hands. "I have served in Lady Ilyra's rooms since before you were born. I did not give Liora those keys. I would swear it on the Flame, on the estate register, on anything this house holds sacred. The fire was a child's mistake. I carried her out of the smoke myself. Ask anyone who saw the stairwell."

"I am not asking, Mistress Fen," Krail says. "I am recording." He turns the order a half-inch so its lines sit square to the table's edge. "Two counts. Unauthorized entry into a sealed apartment of the household. Destruction of household property, including one portrait of considerable sentimental and material value. The folio is a separate matter pending inventory, though her responsibility for the keys bears on it."

"The folio wasn't in those rooms," Elise says. "I never saw a shipping folio in Lady Ilyra's apartment. Not once in six years."

"Then you will not object to an inventory," Krail replies, and there is no satisfaction in his voice, only the dry patience of a man who believes the arithmetic is already finished.

He sets the pen down beside the order, aligned with its edge, and straightens.

"I will withdraw briefly, my lord. The burned apartment should be inventoried before anyone else disturbs it, and the household record for this quarter requires my signature in any case. The order remains here." He taps the paper once with a clean fingernail. "Unsigned. No punishment proceeds without it. If you wish the prisoners held, they are held. If you wish them examined, the east wing physician attends on your word alone — that too requires no countersignature."

At the word *examined*, Elise's chin lifts slightly. Liora looks up at her mother, then at the tall windows, then at the floor, shifting her weight from one scuffed shoe to the other. The blistered palm is curled against her skirt, hidden now, as though hiding it might make the hearing forget it exists.

Krail collects his key ring from the table and fits the case of writing tools back into his coat with two precise motions. At the door he pauses, hand on the latch, and looks back — not at Elise, not at Liora, but at Nera, with that ledger-keeper's attention that weighs and records and files.

"The household watches how the young lord judges, my lord. That is not a threat. It is simply what households do." He inclines his head a precise degree. "I will return within the hour."

The door opens. Cold corridor light crosses the carpet for a moment, and somewhere beyond it — close, closer than a servant should stand — comes the faint creak of someone shifting their weight back from the doorframe. Then the latch clicks shut and the sound is gone.

The room settles into the smell of ash and lamp oil. The ruined portrait leans against the wall, Ilyra's painted face eaten to the chin by flame, one silver eye still intact above the scorch line. Liora stares at it. Her mouth opens — the beginning of an explanation, an apology, something loud and spilling — and Elise's hand presses her shoulder, and the words die unspoken.

Isolde stands where she has stood all along, hands folded, head turned a few degrees toward the closed door. The yellow eyes come back to Nera and wait.

So does everything else in the room: the unsigned order, the pen, the two exhausted women, the burned mother on the wall.
